description: The committed file systems/error-tracking/error-log.json (last touched by an unrelated commit a07a533, not by rebuild-log.py) is invalid JSON -- JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter at line 1725, where the entries array closes and a second unwrapped "metadata": {...}, "entries": [ block begins right after with no enclosing object or comma. This is the same symptom reported as err-20260915T080707-UDZNMO and marked resolved on 2026-09-16 -- but that assessment was wrong: rebuild-log.py itself is not broken. Verified this cycle by running `python3 systems/error-tracking/rebuild-log.py --out /tmp/rebuild-test.json`, which produced valid JSON with 426 correctly-parsed entries on the first try. The actual problem is that the stale, already-corrupted error-log.json sitting in the repo is being read directly (via a bare json.load on the committed file) instead of being regenerated fresh via the script's --out flag before each read -- so the corrupted static artifact keeps reappearing as a 'broken parse' regardless of the script's own health.
correction: Anything that needs the aggregated error log should invoke `python3 systems/error-tracking/rebuild-log.py --out <path>` fresh rather than reading the committed systems/error-tracking/error-log.json directly -- that file is a stale, already-corrupted leftover, not a live regeneration target. Whoever owns this file next should either delete it from the repo (rebuild-log.py's stdout/--out output is the real source of truth and needs no committed cache) or regenerate and commit a clean copy.
systemic_fix: Not applied by this session -- systems/ is a gated directory per SYSTEM.md's Capability Creation Boundary; deleting or regenerating the committed error-log.json is a systems/ change that needs Rigby, not Master/Jarvis. Flagging for Rigby rather than editing directly. Worked around this cycle by reading all 429 individual systems/error-tracking/entries/*.json files directly for the 30-day category tally.
